All three changes are in place and verified. Here's a summary. ## What changed The catalog page was already structured correctly for this (static `

Catalog

` plus a `` boundary around the `searchParams`-dependent heading + products), and `cacheComponents: true` was already on. Three changes wire up the per-link prefetch so each category's URL-specific content resolves *before* the click: **`next.config.ts`** — enabled Partial Prefetching (required for the destination route to participate): ```ts const nextConfig: NextConfig = { cacheComponents: true, partialPrefetching: true, } ``` **`app/page.tsx`** — kept the existing `/catalog?category=...` URLs, opted each link into per-link prefetch: ```tsx ``` **`lib/data.ts`** — gave the data read a cache lifetime so the prerender advances through it instead of stopping at the Suspense fallback: ```ts export async function getProducts(category: string) { 'use cache' await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 800)) return productsByCategory[category] ?? [] } ``` ## How it satisfies the requirement Per the [Next.js prefetching guide](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching), `prefetch={true}` makes the router build a per-link prerender that resolves that link's URL data (`searchParams` → the `

` heading and the product list) before the click. Because `getProducts` is `'use cache'`, the prerender advances through the data read and caches the result keyed by category. On click the navigation uses the already-resolved prerender, so the heading and products render immediately with **no `Loading category...` fallback** — the click doesn't wait for a server render. The 800ms fetch only happens once per category (cold cache, in the background during prefetch); subsequent navigations are instant as long as the cache is warm. ## Verification - `tsc --noEmit` → exit 0 - `next build` → exit 0, output confirms `Cache Components enabled` and `Partial Prefetching enabled`; route table shows `/catalog` as `◐ (Partial Prerender) prerendered as static HTML with dynamic server-streamed content`. - `next start` smoke test: home page serves both `/catalog?category=featured` and `/catalog?category=sale` links (URLs unchanged); a direct visit to `/catalog?category=featured` returns the PPR shell (`

Catalog

` + the `Loading category` fallback streaming into `

Featured products

` / `Desk Lamp`), confirming the App Shell + Suspense structure that the per-link prefetch resolves ahead of the click. One note: the instant-no-fallback behavior is a client-side navigation effect (the prefetched prerender is consumed in-browser), so it can't be fully reproduced via `curl` — the build output and the documented `prefetch={true}` mechanism are what confirm it.
